title: Build SDM Exec Demo HTML Page
spec:
## Task: Build SDM Automation Executive Demo Page

### Output
Single file: `content/sdm-exec-demo/index.html`
Self-contained (all CSS/JS inline or CDN). No backend.

### Purpose
Executive 1:1 tomorrow (25 min). Demonstrates forward-thinking SDM automation vision. Must be deployed to GitHub Pages for a public shareable link.

### Tech Stack (match existing)
- Tailwind CSS CDN
- Alpine.js CDN
- Inter font (Google Fonts)
- Lucide icons (unpkg)
- Cisco brand colors: `#049fd9` (blue), `#171f2d` (dark), `#00bceb` (teal), `#6cc04a` (green)

---

### Page Architecture — 4 Sections, Fixed Nav

**Nav** (sticky top): "SDM AI Transformation" | links: Vision · Live Work · Roadmap · Governance

---

**Section 1: Hero — "The AI-Augmented SDM"**
- Dark gradient background (cisco-dark to navy)
- Badge: "Cisco CX · AI Factory"
- H1: "From Manual Manager to AI-Augmented Leader"
- Subtext: "34 agents. 8 CX roles. Transforming how service delivery works — starting now."
- 3 animated stat cards (white/translucent):
  - "45 min → 5 min" / Weekly Status Report
  - "8 hrs → 30 min" / QBR Preparation  
  - "Reactive → 5 Days Ahead" / Risk Detection
- CTA button: "See What's Live ↓" (scrolls to section 2)

---

**Section 2: Live Work — "Phase 1 Pilots (Active)"**
- Section header: "What's Running Today"
- 3 interactive agent cards in a grid. Each card has:
  - Agent name + role badge
  - Status pill: "🟡 In Design" 
  - One-line description
  - Click to expand: trigger, what it reads, output, time saved, trust tier
- Agent 1: **Delivery Tracker** (SDM · T1)
  - Trigger: Daily 7am
  - Reads: Helix API — milestones, cases, entitlements
  - Output: Ranked account health dashboard
  - Time saved: 45 min manual pull → 5 min review
  - Trust tier: T1 — read-only, no approval needed
- Agent 2: **Risk & Escalation Sentinel** (SDM · T2)
  - Trigger: Daily 8am (after Delivery Tracker)
  - Detects: P1/P2 open >48h, SLA breach predicted <5 days, health drop >15pts
  - Output: Webex card with [Escalate] [Schedule Call] [Snooze] [Dismiss] — human approves
  - Time saved: Reactive detection → 5–10 days predictive lead time
  - Trust tier: T2 — HITL gate, human approves before any action
- Agent 3: **Business Review Generator** (SDM/CXM · T2)
  - Trigger: On-demand CLI per account
  - Reads: Salesforce, ServiceNow, Helix, Delivery Tracker
  - Output: Full QBR draft — exec summary, delivery narrative, risk section, next quarter priorities
  - Time saved: 8–12 hrs QBR prep → 30 min review + edit
  - Trust tier: T2 — SDM reviews all sections, agent never sends autonomously

---

**Section 3: The Factory — "6-Phase Roadmap"**
- Horizontal timeline (desktop) / vertical (mobile) showing 6 phases
- Phase 0: Foundation ✅ (Governance, baselines, agent cards)
- Phase 1: SDM Pilots 🟡 (Weeks 5–12 · 3 agents · Proof of model)
- Phase 2: CXM + PM (Months 4–6 · 7 agents · Customer health, plan mgmt)
- Phase 3: CE + CDA (Months 7–9 · 8 agents · Config & architecture acceleration)
- Phase 4: HTOM + SDM Ops (Months 10–12 · 8 agents · SLA, resources, entitlements)
- Phase 5: CPM + CXL (Year 2 Q1 · 8 agents · Program intelligence, exec reporting)
- Phase 6: Orchestration (Year 2 Q2+ · Agent chains · End-to-end automation)
- End state callout box: "34 agents · 8 roles · 40–80% cycle-time reduction per workflow"
- 4 example agent chains (collapsible):
  - Account Risk-to-Action: Health Pulse → Risk Sentinel → Outreach Drafter
  - QBR Factory: Delivery Tracker → Entitlement Monitor → Business Review Generator → Exec Report
  - Technical Delivery Accelerator: Pattern Matcher → Compatibility Validator → Design Doc Generator
  - Operations Intelligence Loop: Risk Radar → SLA Sentinel → Resource Optimizer → Org Dashboard

---

**Section 4: Governance — "Built to Be Trusted"**
- Section header: "Human Control Is the Architecture, Not an Afterthought"
- 3-column trust tier cards:
  - **T1 — Read & Summarize**: Reads data, surfaces insights. No approval needed. Agent displays; human decides.
  - **T2 — Draft + Human Gate**: Agent drafts action. Webex card. Human approves before anything happens. 45-day monitored window.
  - **T3 — Autonomous**: Only after 45-day HITL evidence, false positive rate <20%, GRC sign-off. Not used yet.
- HITL flow diagram (CSS-drawn): Agent generates → Webex card → Human reviews → [Approve/Edit/Dismiss/Snooze] → All decisions logged
- Principles row (4 icons): "Audit Before Build" · "Draft First" · "Extend What Exists" · "One Chain, One Metric"
- Footer: "Governance log maintained in AI_FACTORY_GOVERNANCE_LOG.md · Phase gate reviews every sprint"

---

### Interactions
- Sticky nav with active section highlighting (Intersection Observer)
- Section 2 agent cards: click to expand/collapse details (Alpine.js x-show)
- Section 3 phase timeline: click phase to highlight and show agent list
- Section 3 chains: click to expand
- Smooth scroll throughout
- All data is hardcoded static — no API calls, no user input

### Security (CodeGuard compliant)
- No innerHTML with dynamic data — all content is hardcoded static strings
- No eval, no dynamic code execution
- All external CDN scripts use SRI integrity hashes
- textContent for any dynamic DOM (Alpine bindings on static data only)
- rel="noopener noreferrer" on any external links
- No localStorage, no cookies, no session state (static page)

---

### GitHub Pages Deployment Steps (append to bottom of file as HTML comment)
```
<!-- DEPLOYMENT:
1. git add content/sdm-exec-demo/index.html
2. git commit -m "Add SDM exec demo page"
3. git push origin main
4. In GitHub repo Settings > Pages > Source: Deploy from branch > main > /root
5. URL will be: https://{username}.github.io/{repo}/content/sdm-exec-demo/
-->
```

### Files to Read Before Building
- `content/ai-factory/index.html` (lines 1–100) — match this exact CSS/Tailwind/Alpine pattern
- `AI_FACTORY_AGENT_REGISTRY.md` — agent names, phases, trust tiers
- `AI_FACTORY_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` — KPI targets, phase descriptions, agent chain definitions (sections 1, 6, 11, 15)

### Report Back
Confirm file created at `content/sdm-exec-demo/index.html` and provide the GitHub Pages URL after push.
